hypotheses.paper: 1°, second sentence: P n'est autre que l'image réciproque par φ̃ de l'ensemble des points où z < 1
hypotheses.note: Proved in its component form (poche_eq_connectedComponentIn_affine: P is the connected component of each of its points in φ̃⁻¹{z < 1}). The full form is proved equivalent to the connectedness of {z < 1} ∩ φ̃(V), for one V (poche_eq_preimage_iff_affine) and for the printed statement (premierAffinePrinted_iff). It is proved for z ≡ 0, the only constant cote. It is proved when φ̃(V) is star-shaped about a point of cote < 1, so when it is convex. It is proved in every dimension n ≤ 1 (premierAffinePrinted_of_le_one). It is open for a non-constant cote in dimension n ≥ 2. See findings.

findings: 1°c, the full form (statement l.632–633), is not proved for a non-constant cote in dimension n ≥ 2, and it is not refuted. This is the affine twin of OQ-71. The proof is « comme le précédent » (l.644–645), so its 1°c is the projective l.585–590. There, l.588 (« on peut construire dans D ∩ φ̃(V) une ligne brisée ») presumes D ∩ φ̃(V) connected. The forward reference (l.184–186, « resp. affine ») claims only « une composante connexe ». What is proved: (i) the component form; (ii) the full form is exactly the connectedness of {z < 1} ∩ φ̃(V), for one V (poche_eq_preimage_iff_affine) and for the printed statement (premierAffinePrinted_iff : PremierAffinePrinted n ↔ ConnexeAffinePrinted n); (iii) the full form for z ≡ 0, which is the only constant cote (IsPocheAff.cote_eq_zero_of_linear_eq_zero); (iv) the full form when φ̃(V) is star-shaped about a point of cote < 1, in particular when it is convex (poche_eq_preimage_of_starConvex_affine, poche_eq_preimage_of_convex_affine); 3° gives convexity for a shell; (v) the printed full form in every dimension n ≤ 1, where φ̃(V) is an interval or a point (premierAffinePrinted_of_le_one); (vi) a witness with a non-constant cote and P ≠ V, the half-space {x₀ > 0} ⊂ ℝⁿ⁺¹ (theoreme_premier_affine_demiEspace). Argued, not formalised: the full form also holds when φ̃(V) is a cone, that is, invariant under the positive homotheties h_t of one centre c, with c ∉ φ̃(V) allowed. Suppose z(c) ≥ 1. Then for x ∈ P, the ray h_t(x), t ≥ 1, stays in φ̃(V) ∩ {z < 1} and so in P, while z → −∞ along it, against inf z = 0. So z(c) < 1. Then any path of φ̃(V) between two points of {z < 1}, contracted towards c, joins them inside {z < 1}. A counterexample therefore needs n ≥ 2, and φ̃(V) can be neither a cone nor star-shaped about a point of cote < 1.

1°c, the inclusion P ⊆ φ̃⁻¹{z < 1}. This is proof level; the statement is unaffected. The proof, « comme le précédent », i.e. l.585–590, does not argue it. Condition a of Déf. 1 (l.106–107) gives only « majorée par 1 ». The inclusion holds because φ(P) is open, and an affine function reaching its supremum 1 at an interior point is constant, which contradicts inf z = 0 (IsPocheAff.cote_lt_one).

1°b, inherited from the projective proof (l.568–570, the bracket « puisque GS(n, R) opère transitivement sur la fibre des jets de même source, il existe γ … »). This is proof level; the statement is unaffected. With GA(n, ℝ) in place of GS(n, ℝ), transitivity on fibres gives γ at each point only. A single γ for all of V needs V connected and the rigidity of GA(n, ℝ) (IsDeveloping.existsUnique_smul_eq). The bracket names neither.

OQ-46, bearing only, deciding nothing. In the affine Theorem's situation (V connected, sweepable, with one pocket), every developing map is injective. So the affine example of § 1 (l.155–166) holds there without the injectivity that exemple_poche_affine carries (exemple_poche_affine_of_poche). The affine reading of the forward reference (l.183–186) holds too (situation_exemple_affine). The examples themselves concern an arbitrary étalé W, which is untouched.
questions: « induisant φ sur P » (l.631–632). The affine 1° does not print it, and the scan (journal p. 256) agrees with the transcription. The projective 1° prints it (l.522–523). The affine 1°'s second sentence needs it: z is a function on the target of φ, and only EqOn φ̃ φ P ties it to φ̃. The proof is « comme le précédent ». Reading taken: present. Every statement here carries EqOn φ̃ φ P, which is stronger than the literal text. The literal reading (some compatible chart φ̃ with source V and P = φ̃⁻¹({z < 1} ∩ φ̃(V)), with no EqOn) is stated as PremierAffineLiteralPrinted n, and PremierAffinePrinted.literal shows it follows from the reading taken. Whether the literal form is the statement of record is the author's decision.

1°'s second sentence (l.632–633, « P n'est autre que l'image réciproque par φ̃ de l'ensemble des points où z < 1 ») against the forward reference (l.184–186, « P n'est autre qu'une composante connexe de l'image réciproque », resp. affine). This is the affine twin of OQ-71. Reading taken: the component form is proved as the formalisation's claim (PremierComposanteAffinePrinted n, for every n). The printed full form is stated as PremierAffinePrinted n and is proved equivalent to ConnexeAffinePrinted n. It is proved for n ≤ 1, for z ≡ 0, and for a star-shaped or convex φ̃(V). It is open otherwise. Neither form has been made the formalisation of record; the mark follows OQ-71's answer.

« une application φ̃ de V sur S(n) » (l.538, l.559), read with ℝⁿ for S(n) as l.644–645 instructs. « sur » is read « dans » (into), as in the projective file. The onto reading is false on the half-space witness, where φ̃(V) is the half-space and not ℝⁿ. 1° itself says « sur un ouvert de ℝⁿ ».

kb_proposals: Chapter 2 § 3's 1°a and 1°b for any (G, X): Benzecri.PremierGX (Chapter2/PremierAffine.lean). They need only a compatible chart φ with connected source P and hmove : ∀ E, IsCompact E → ∃ g : GXAut G X M, g • E ⊆ P, plus [PreconnectedSpace M] [LocPathConnectedSpace M] [IsAnalyticAction G X]. They give the developing map equal to φ on P (exists_isDeveloping_eqOn), injectivity of every developing map (injective_of_isDeveloping), the chart (exists_chart_eqOn) and uniqueness (eq_of_eqOn). Feed hmove from Prop. 7 or 7′ with G := ⊤. The projective Developpement.lean could be rederived from them.

The affine closure step needs no hemisphere. Take a ball inside {z < 1} ∩ range φ̃ (Metric.isOpen_iff), a point of P over it (mem_closure_iff), convex_ball.segment_subset, then isAffSegment_of_chart (the affine twin of isProjSegment_of_chart) and condition b with ψ := φ̃. For z ≡ 0 the pocket is then clopen, so P = V, with no twin of closure_poche_subset_preimage_hemisphere.

Sufficient conditions for the full form of 1°c (P = φ̃⁻¹({z < 1} ∩ φ̃(V))): φ̃(V) star-shaped about a c with z c < 1, via ((convex_Iio 1).affine_preimage z).starConvex hc |>.inter hstar |>.isPathConnected; or φ̃(V) convex; or n ≤ 1, where convex_of_isPreconnected_of_le_one goes through ContinuousLinearEquiv.funUnique (Fin 1) ℝ ℝ and Mathlib's IsPreconnected.convex on ℝ.

A constant cote of an affine pocket is 0: IsPocheAff.cote_eq_zero_of_linear_eq_zero, from isGLB_singleton.unique. The cote is < 1 on an affine pocket: IsPocheAff.cote_lt_one, a direct proof in ℝⁿ that does not pass through toPocheProj.
